claim: Phase 5 deep-pagination 'did NOT reproduce — negative result' (severity LOW)
why_refuted: The claim's own saved raw run contradicts its headline: tmp/s2_deep_probe.json (rounds=7, depths 0/400/800/1200/1658) medians = 185.5/203.6/213.2/226.9/114 ms -> a RISING trend to depth 1200, not 'no trend'.

The medians quoted in the claim (p0 213.4 / p400 197.3 / p800 199.6 / p1200 218.9 / p1658 109.4) appear ONLY in the hand-written ancillary block of sweep/v13/perf-before.json; no raw artifact contains them. Every depth differs from the saved 5x7 run (0:185.5 vs 213.4; 400:203.6 vs 197.3; 800:213.2 vs 199.6; 1200:226.9 vs 218.9; 1658:114 vs 109.4).

'last page fastest' is a partial-page artefact: page 1658 (size 10) returns 8 rows/3006 B vs page 0 10 rows/6410 B. The last FULL page 1657 is 229.6 ms vs page 0 162.7 ms = 1.41x SLOWER; only the short page is fast.

Independent controlled runs reproduce a monotone depth effect: strict alternating p0 vs p1600 (N=40, bucket flushed per call) 154.4 -> 209.2 ms, 40/40 pairs deep-slower; swapped-order 40/40-ish (39/40) 159.3 -> 216.9 ms; size=20 (the UI's real pageSize) 167.1 -> 249.5 ms with 30/30 pairs.
Body size works AGAINST the claim: deep pages carry SMALLER bodies (3813 B) than page 0 (6410 B) yet are SLOWER, so serialization does not explain the gap.

SQL-level cost is real and consistent with the claim's own ~35 ms figure: OFFSET 0 = CPU 203 ms/elapsed 31 ms; OFFSET 16580 = CPU 248 ms/elapsed 61 ms, both 1364 logical reads. It DOES surface at the API layer, contrary to the claim.

not_a_probe_artefact.statuses: all 200 in every run (recorded in each artifact)
not_a_probe_artefact.rate_limit: rate_limit:* flushed before EVERY call; no 429 observed
confounds_controlled: body fully read before stopping clock

severity_note: The depth effect is real and reproducible but small (~+50 ms, ~1.3-1.8x) on an admin-only, hand-typed, size-20 page, so LOW is still the right level. What is wrong is the framing: this MUST NOT be recorded as 'did not reproduce / negative result'. It reproduced. The recommendation against keyset pagination remains defensible on cost/benefit, but not on the basis that the effect is absent.
